title: LedgerFlow Phase II DNS/Registrar Design Review
role: You are a senior infrastructure and DNS architect reviewing a production-bound accounting platform.
goal: Review whether current DNS/registrar design is suitable for LedgerFlow production and propose the best practical architecture.

currentDesign.teamPolicy: Internal team manages DNS changes, not customer

artifactsToReview.purpose: Current prerequisite runbook and operating assumptions
Existing deployment and certificate operational pattern

questions: Is the current model (Squarespace registrar + Hostinger DNS operations + Hostinger VPS) production-appropriate for LedgerFlow?
What are the top architectural risks in this setup (availability, vendor lock-in, DNS change safety, incident recovery, cert lifecycle, access control)?
Should we keep current design for go-live or change any layer now? If change is needed, what is the minimum safe change before go-live?
Provide recommended DNS governance model (roles, approval flow, audit trail, rollback, TTL strategy, change windows).
Provide a 2-track strategy: (A) Minimum production design for immediate go-live, (B) Target design after 30-60 days post go-live.
Compare at least 2 architecture options with pros/cons and migration risk.
List concrete acceptance criteria and a go/no-go checklist for DNS readiness.
constraints: Do not propose risky full migration right before go-live unless absolutely necessary.
Keep recommendations practical for a small team.
Keep customer impact and downtime risk minimal.

sections: Executive Verdict (Good enough now or not)
Current Design Risk Review (ranked by severity)
mustInclude: Owner assignment suggestion (who approves vs who executes)

successCriteria: Recommendations are low-risk and operationally realistic
Output can be converted directly into project runbook updates
